rationale: Start with a broad mid-temperature scouting gradient to elute all 8 compounds and reveal the overall retention window without much risk of truncation. This gives a baseline on where peaks fall and whether the main limitation is selectivity or run time.

Only one pair is limiting and all peaks elute comfortably within 10 min, so first test whether that pair is slope-sensitive by making the gradient much shallower while keeping the same phi window and temperature. If the critical pair opens markedly, we can later recover speed by trimming tG; if not, we will know to shift temperature or the phi window instead.

The critical pair is strongly slope-sensitive: tG = 40 fully resolves everything but is too slow, while tG = 20 is too steep. Try an intermediate tG near the expected threshold for full resolution, keeping the same window and temperature since all compounds already elute within 10 min at tG = 20.

The critical pair improves steadily with shallower slope, and tG = 24 is still below the full-resolution threshold while only slightly over 10 min. Test tG = 28 to approach the minimum gradient time that gets the last pair to R at least 1.5 with a smaller time penalty than tG = 40.

The critical pair is not being fixed efficiently enough by slope alone, so probe temperature next: lowering T should increase retention and can change selectivity enough to open a close pair while still keeping the run likely under 10–12 min from the tG = 20 baseline. This tells us whether T can rescue the pair more economically than a much longer gradient.

At 25 C the difficult selectivity is much improved and only one pair sits slightly below 1.5, so first try to cut time modestly while seeing whether that pair remains acceptable. If resolution holds, this could move closer to the best possible CRF by bringing the last peak nearer to 10 min.

The best region is clearly around 25 C, and the limiting pair at tG = 20 is only slightly under the 1.5 target, so a small increase in tG should lift it to full credit with only a modest time penalty. This is the most likely route to exceed the current best CRF.

At 25 C and tG = 20 we are close to optimal, so now trim the high-end window slightly to make the effective gradient shallower in the peak region and potentially improve the near-critical pair without adding as much time as increasing tG.
